  CITY COUNCIL

Tuesday, November 14, 2023  7:00 PM  Council Chambers

NOTE:  PUBLIC PARTICIPATION INFORMATION
  Agenda reports and other disclosable public records relating to each Open Session agenda item are
  available on the City's website under City Council Meeting agendas at rhe.city and during regular
  business hours in the office of the City Clerk. Meetings are live broadcast on the City's website and a
  recording is available for viewing after each meeting. Meetings are also broadcast on PVP-TV Channel 35
  (Cox) and Channel 39 (Verizon).

  Public Comment is welcome in-person on any item during City Council consideration of the item. Public
  correspondence may also be emailed to the City Clerk at laurenp@rollinghillsestates.gov. Emails
  received before 3:00 p.m. prior to the start of the meeting will be forwarded to the City Council for their
  consideration and included as part of the record. Members of the public may also comment online using
  eComment on the “Meeting Agendas, Minutes & Videos” page of the City’s website
  (www.rhe.city/MeetingAgendas). Once the agenda is published, there will be an “eComment” button next
  to the linked agenda under "Upcoming Events". Follow this link to the City’s SpeakUp page. After you
  register, you may comment on any item on that particular agenda. These comments can be seen by the
  public, will be considered by the Council and become part of the record.

  An opportunity is also provided for the public to comment on non-agenda items concerning City matters. If
  you would like to address the City Council regarding an item on this agenda or make a general public
  comment, please complete a speaker sheet and give to the City Clerk.

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

4.  CEREMONIAL ITEMS

  A.  PROCLAMATION:  DECLARING  NOVEMBER  25,  2023 AS  "SMALL
  BUSINESS SATURDAY"
  Attachments: Proclamation

5.  CONSENT CALENDAR
  The following routine matters will be acted upon by one vote to approve with the majority consent of the
  City Council. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless good cause is shown by a member
  prior to the roll call vote. (Items removed for individual consideration will be voted on separately.)

  A.  READING OF ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS
  Reading in full of all ordinances and resolutions presented for consideration to the
  City Council will be waived and all such ordinances and resolutions will be read by
  title only.
  B.  DEMANDS AND WARRANTS OF OCTOBER 2023
  Recommendation: Approve warrants 66760 through 66824 in the amount of
  $152,194.33; and Supplemental Warrants 100423 through 100523; 110123 through
  110323; in the amount of $212,472.77; for a grand total amount of $364,667.10
  with proper audit.
  Attachments: Demands & Warrants

  C.  CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF OCTOBER 24, 2023
  Recommendation: Review and approve.
  Attachments: Draft Minutes

  D.  PLANNING COMMISSION MINUTES OF NOVEMBER 6, 2023
  Recommendation: Receive and file.
  Attachments: Draft Minutes

  E.  NOTICE OF COMPLETION - FISCAL YEAR 2023-24 STRAWBERRY AND
  DAPPLEGRAY LANES RE-SURFACING PROJECT BY HARDY & HARPER,
  INC.
  Recommendation: That the City Council 1) Accept the re-surfacing of Strawberry
  Lane and berm resurfacing of Dapplegray, Buckskin and Sorrel Lanes’ project as
  complete, 2) Authorize the City Clerk to file the Notice of Completion form with the
  Los Angeles County Recorder’s Office on November 15, 2023, and 3) If no claims
  are filed within 35 days after recordation, direct staff to release the 5% construction
  retention payment to Hardy & Harper, Inc. in the amount of $28,898.68.
  Attachments: Staff Report

  F.  SOUTH BAY CITIES COUNCIL OF GOVERNMENTS BOARD MEETING
  HIGHLIGHTS OF OCTOBER 2023
  Recommendation: Receive and File
  Attachments: Staff Report

6.  PUBLIC COMMENT / PUBLIC PRESENTATIONS
  This is the appropriate time for members of the public to make comments regarding items not listed on this
  agenda. If you would like to address the City Council, please complete a speaker sheet and give to the
  City Clerk. Under the State's open meeting law - the Brown Act - no action may be taken on any item not
  on the agenda.

  A.  WASTE MANAGEMENT "RECYCLING HERO" DRAWING FOR ONE YEAR

8.  NEW BUSINESS

**ADJOURN TO PEPPER TREE FOUNDATION BOARD MEETING**

  A.  PEPPER  TREE  FOUNDATION  LARGE  DONOR  FUNDRAISING
  CAMPAIGN FOR  NATURE CENTER PROJECT AND ASSOCIATED
  NAMING POLICY
  Memorandum from Alexa Davis, Assistant City Manager
  Recommendation: That the Pepper Tree Foundation Board of Directors review,
  provide input, and approve 1) the conceptual proposal of the large donor campaign
  for the George F Canyon Nature Center project; and 2) the “Peppertree Foundation
  Funded Capital Project Naming Policy.”
  Attachments: Staff Report

** RECONVENE CITY COUNCIL MEETING **

  B.  COMMEMORATING  INDIGENOUS  PEOPLE  AND  JAPANESE
  AMERICANS OF PALOS VERDES PENINSULA
  Memorandum from Alexa Davis, Assistant City Manager
  Recommendation: That the City Council provide input, and direct staff on how to
  proceed with the proposed projects commemorating the history of Indigenous People
  and Japanese Americans of Rolling Hills Estates.
  Attachments: Staff Report

9.  OLD BUSINESS

  NONE

10.  CITY ATTORNEY ITEMS

11.  CITY COUNCIL / REGIONAL COMMITTEE REPORTS
  This item provides the opportunity for Members of the City Council to provide information and reports to
  other Members of the City Council and the public on any issues or activities of Council Committees, ad
  hoc committees, regional or state-wide governmental associations, special districts, joint powers
  authorities and the various committees on which Members of the City Council might serve or have an
  interest, which are not otherwise agendized.

12.  MAYOR AND COUNCIL ITEMS
  This item provides the opportunity for Members of the City Council to request information on currently
  pending projects and/or issues of public concern, direct that an item be agendized for future consideration
  and/or make announcements of interest to the public.
